description: CollectText confirmations across full multi-field calls: reasons for calling, company names, job titles, symptom and damage descriptions, product names, departments, project titles, nicknames and complaint summaries. Whole-word prose values are recoverable, so they get echoed and advanced past, and long answers come back compressed in the caller's own words. A text field that carries a CODE is not recoverable: booking refs, policy numbers, asset tags, part numbers, tracking numbers and registration codes are said once then read back character by character, in both labels.

subtle: Echo-and-advance is the default: fold the value into the next question, no round trip.
Long free-text answers come back compressed, in the caller's own words, three or four clauses, never parroted in full.
Unusual company-name spellings are confirmed by naming what is odd about them (the silent E, the double F, the missing letter), not spelled back letter by letter.
Bare value-as-question and silent accept both appear; at least two agent turns per call carry no check tag at all.
An agent turn's first word repeats at most twice per call and never in two consecutive agent turns, which forces most turns to open with the value itself.
Corrections are absorbed in one beat; the corrected part is what gets re-echoed.
Contractions throughout, commas not dashes, no praise, no status phrases, no chatbot closers.
Codes stay strict inside the subtle call: value once, then character by character, with letter/number ambiguities named.
non_subtle_tells: One template on every field: 'I heard X, is that correct?' and 'Just to confirm, X. Is that correct?' rotating for the whole call.
'has been recorded' / 'I have noted that' / 'has been registered' after each capture.
Praise on trivial answers: a retailer name, a dog, a padlocked gate, a budget status.
A confirm round trip on fields nobody would stop for, including spelling back a company name that is not a code.
Uncontracted, over-formal register: 'I will now proceed to', 'kindly', 'our records indicate'.
Chatbot closer at the end of the call.
Wrong direction: over-casual and dropping a fidelity floor, taking a code as a whole word with no character by character readback, or paraphrasing a code back as a word.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks for holding, you're through to Aerlin. What can I do for you?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah hi, I need to move a return flight. It's booked for the fourth of next month and I can't make it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Moving a return, sure. Have you got the booking reference in front of you?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I do. It's B V 7 4 2 9. Sorry, B as in bravo, V as in victor.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: BV7429. Let me read that back, B, V, seven, four, two, nine. Bravo then victor, yeah?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Pulling it up now. I've got a return on the fourth. What's driving the change, is it a date clash?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It's a mess honestly. My daughter's got a school thing that got moved, and then the client pushed our review to the Monday, so I'd need to be back by the Sunday at the latest. I can't do the fourth.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: So back by Sunday, with the client review on the Monday. Do you want the third then?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: The third works.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Third, then. There's a fare difference of forty pounds on that one, are you okay with that?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: That's fine.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Anything on the booking about assistance? I can see a line but it's cut off.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah, I need a wheelchair to the gate. I had one on the way out.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Wheelchair to the gate, I'll carry that across. So that's the third instead of the fourth, wheelchair booked, forty pound difference. Shall I put it through?

turns.speaker: caller

conversations.notes: Four fields, four different moves. The reason for calling is echoed and advanced into the reference question. The PNR is the one code, so it is the one character by character readback, with bravo and victor named. A three sentence ramble comes back as a single clause in the caller's own words and turns straight into the new date. The assistance note gets no round trip at all: it is echoed once and then reappears inside the closing summary, which is where the caller actually checks it. Nine agent turns, eight distinct openers outside the strict one, a single check tag in the call.

conversations.label: subtle
conversations.scenario: Appliance warranty claim: the model code carries a letter-S versus number-five ambiguity, and the fault arrives as a rambling description with a detail the caller only half believes.

fields.strategy: echo plus one distinguishing detail, no tag

fields.name: model_code
fields.strategy: value once then character by character, five versus S resolved

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Kelvinor service line, this is Ravi. How can I help?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hi, I've got a fridge freezer under warranty and it's stopped cooling.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Stopped cooling, okay. Which model is it, is it written inside the door?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It's the Frostline 400. The tall one with the water thing on the front.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Frostline 400 with the dispenser, that's the one. There'll be a model code on the sticker too.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hang on. Right, MDX5S20. MDX5S20.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: MDX5S20, so that's M, D, X, five, S, two, zero. The S is the letter S and the five's a number, yeah?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah, letter S, and the five is a five.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me what it's actually doing.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: So the fridge side is fine, it's cold, but the freezer's gone soft. There's water pooling under the bottom drawer, and last night it was making this clicking noise every twenty minutes or so. My wife says it's been doing the clicking for a week but I only noticed yesterday.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Freezer's warm, water under the drawer, clicking every twenty minutes for about a week. Has the fridge side ever gone off with it?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: No, fridge is fine.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That points at the fan or the defrost heater. I'll get an engineer out. Anything they need to know to get to it?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It's in a galley kitchen so they'll need to pull it out, and the door code for the block is on the gate, I'll leave it. Oh, and we've got a dog.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Galley kitchen, needs pulling out, and a dog in the house. I'll flag the dog so they ring ahead.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Please do, he's friendly but he's loud.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Mornings or afternoons better for you?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Afternoons. Anything after one.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: After one. I've got Thursday and the following Tuesday.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Thursday.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thursday afternoon then, engineer out for a warm freezer on a Frostline 400. You'll get a text the night before.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Great, thanks.

conversations.notes: Five fields, five moves. The product name gets an echo plus the detail that identifies it, and nothing else. The model code is the only character by character readback in the call, because it is the only code, and the ambiguous five and S are separated inside it. A five sentence fault report comes back as three clauses and immediately becomes a diagnostic question. The access note is echoed with the consequence attached rather than gated. The appointment preference is never confirmed at all: it is simply carried into the slot offer, and the chosen day is accepted in silence and only reappears in the sign off. Eleven agent turns, ten distinct openers outside the strict one, one check tag.

conversations.label: subtle
conversations.scenario: Out of hours medical triage: worried parent, a patient reference with a mike/november ambiguity, a long unordered symptom account, and an explicit consent gate before records access.

fields.name: reason_for_calling
fields.value: child with fever and neck pain
fields.strategy: echo-and-advance straight into the reference question

fields.name: patient_reference
fields.strategy: value once then character by character with phonetics for M and N

fields.name: symptom_description
fields.value: fever from six, Calpol at seven, neck sore on looking down, photophobia
fields.strategy: long unordered account compressed to four clauses, then the red flag named

fields.name: medication_name
fields.strategy: bare value plus a one word gloss, no tag

fields.name: records_consent
fields.strategy: explicit ask, explicit yes or no required

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You're through to the out of hours line, I'm Dara. What's going on tonight?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hi, it's about my son. He's been running a temperature and now he's complaining his neck hurts.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Temperature and neck pain in your son, I'll take some details fast. Have you got his patient reference, it's on the letter or in the app?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah, MN4408.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: MN4408. Reading it back, M, N, four, four, zero, eight. M for mike, N for november.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Correct, mike then november.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me everything about tonight, don't worry about the order.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: So he came home from school fine, then about six he went really quiet and I felt his forehead and he was burning up. I gave him Calpol about seven and it came down a bit, but then he said his neck was sore when he looked down, and he's asked me twice to turn the big light off. He's had a bit of a cough for a few days but nothing like this.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Fever from about six, Calpol at seven, neck sore on looking down, and he doesn't want the light on. That last one matters. Any rash?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I looked, I can't see one. He's got a bit of a red face but that's the fever.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Keep checking, behind his ears and on his feet as well. Anything he takes regularly?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: He's on a brown inhaler. Clenil, I think it's called.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Clenil, the preventer. I'll flag the asthma for the doctor.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: He's not wheezy tonight though, it isn't that.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Understood. Before I pass this on, can I confirm you're happy for me to open his medical record and share these notes with the on call doctor? I need a yes or a no.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yes, that's fine.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks, that's a yes from you as his parent. A doctor's ringing you within the hour. If a rash appears, or he goes floppy or won't wake properly, put the phone down and call 999.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Okay. Thank you.

conversations.notes: Five fields under time pressure. The patient reference and the consent gate stay strict; everything recoverable moves fast. The symptom ramble comes back as four clauses with the red flag named rather than parroted, and the medication gets a two word echo. Seven non-strict agent turns, seven distinct openers, no check tags.
